- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.27) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.27) and recent prices are trending down.
- Avoid sharp upward forecasts after recent spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- Adjust downward if true outcome shows mean reversion within 3–5 days after a forecasted peak.
- Reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is low or flat; avoid overfitting to recent highs.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price fails to rise beyond forecast, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for market saturation.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust remaining forecast downward linearly to match observed trend.
